name: Jezero crater
scientificRationale: Jezero preserves a delta interpreted as the remnant of an ancient river entering a lake. NASA's cited Mastcam-Z image description grounds this regional context.

name: Belva crater
scientificRationale: Perseverance's Mastcam-Z observations of Belva show exposed bedrock cross-sections that provide clues to the region's geologic history. NASA discusses dipping beds as a possible ancient sandbar interpretation.
observationContext: NASA's cited panorama was acquired April 22, 2023 (sol 772). This does not date the coordinate record or current map imagery.
coordinateAttribution: International Astronomical Union Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature; Gazetteer maintained by USGS Astrogeology
limitations: The marker represents the published crater center, not Echo Creek or the position where the rover acquired the panorama.
The source publishes center coordinates to two decimal places; no sub-pixel or metre positional accuracy is claimed.
MDIM 2.1 feature geometry is not independently registered to the preliminary CTX mosaic.
No distance, slope, terrain safety, or routing follows from this record.

name: Neretva Vallis
scientificRationale: Neretva is an ancient river channel that fed water into Jezero crater. NASA's Mastcam-Z panorama provides mission context for exploring the channel.
observationContext: NASA's cited panorama was acquired May 17, 2024 (sol 1152). This does not date the coordinate record or current map imagery.
coordinateAttribution: International Astronomical Union Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature; Gazetteer maintained by USGS Astrogeology
limitations: The marker represents the published valley center, not Bright Angel, Mount Washburn, or a precise rover target.
The geographic feature spans a valley; one center does not represent its complete footprint.
